newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks strong at noon, Telefonica off highs.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks strong at noon, Telefonica off highs.

text.p: Madrid stocks were strongly higher at midday on a continued inflow of funds into the market suppported by bond market gains, dealers said.
Telefonica came swiftly off highs after Standard & Poor's said it downgraded the firm's outlook to "negative" from "stable", maintaining its long-term "AA-" debt rating.
As the shares fell buyers stepped in, bringing the stock up 20 pesetas to 4,295, off an intraday high of 4,345 pesetas.
The general index was up 6.59 points, 1.16 percent, to 573.40 while the Ibex-35 was up 83.49 points, 1.28 percent, to 6,597.97.
There was little corporate news pushing stocks up, but buyers were in evidence helped by bond market gains and an easing of tension surrounding EMU, dealers said.

"No-one is selling, so even if there were a limited amount of buyers prices would be going up sharply. A strong economic outlook (at home) is nothing new, although it will always be a factor in the market's favour," said a dealer.
Final foreign investors will likely await next week's EU summit, with a hoped-for clarification of the outlook for the single currency, before making further moves in the bourse, dealers said.
